summary: Keep Labs has begun shipping its first consumer product, the Keep, a lockable smart container that stores medicine and tracks use via a scale and app. The company lost a CES 2020 innovation award over cannabis marketing, then dropped the cannabis messaging for "medicine". After COVID cancelled its manufacturing contracts, it brought in pharmacist Jeff Wandzura as CEO and pivoted toward enterprise medication adherence partnerships, with a cooling second-generation device planned.
one_line: Keep Labs, which lost a CES 2020 award over cannabis marketing, now ships a $299 smart medicine lockbox and pursues healthcare enterprise deals.
key_facts: Keep Labs launched in 2019, won and then lost an innovation award at CES 2020, and this week began shipping its first product to consumers.
The Keep holds about six pill bottles, opens via an app button or a double tap when secure mode is disabled, and uses a scale to detect bottles returned lighter after doses are taken.
The CES award was rescinded because the device was marketed as a cannabis storage device; the CTIA pulled the prize, then softened its stance on cannabis-adjacent products.

Keep Labs now markets the Keep as for "medicine" because Google and Meta restrict the term "cannabis" in advertising, and Kickstarter and Indiegogo disallowed it, so preorders ran through a Shopify store.
Philip Wilkins conceived the Keep after his wife worried their three-year-old would get into his medication.
A preorder campaign launched in December 2019 drew over 15,000 preorders, with 5,000 paying in full; only 5% were canceled after refunds were offered when COVID hit and the manufacturer was lost.

After talking to preorder customers, Keep Labs learned many bought the Keep for medication tracking rather than locking medicine away, leading Wilkins to step down as CEO in favor of Jeff Wandzura, a trained pharmacist who previously sold two digital health companies.
The company has a beta program with 150 users, and customers also store keys, passports and cash in the Keep.

Keep Labs joined the McKesson Digital Health Network in Canada and partners with Savvy Cooperative to give free devices to patients with chronic conditions; enterprise customers pay a nominal subscription fee for de-identified aggregate adherence data.
Keep Labs says it follows HIPAA and PIPEDA, uses TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, and PBKDF2 with SHA256 for password hashing.

Keep Labs has raised $2.18 million from investors including StartUp Health's Transformer Fund, Plug and Play Tech Center, Onbelay Capital and 001 Ventures, and may raise again at the end of 2023 or early 2024.
The second-generation Keep will add cooling, since nearly 50% of drugs in the FDA pipeline require cooling, with Ozempic cited as an example.
The first-generation Keep costs $299, comes in black and white, and is sold on the Keep Labs website.
